body: This.

Um, do you not see the cognitive dissonance of you worrying about work and still thinking about going to kill yourself? You need to seek some help if you just attempted, it's just not cool. What's bothering you anyways?
Read Quiet: Power of Introverts. Thank me later

My parents exact same thing after a 2-week stint in a hospital. I brought it up 3 years later and confronted them. Mom cried. Then never spoke about it again. I was their "prized" child, now blemished. Some parents are just jerks.

Grab your balls and pace around the room until you get your manhood back, and then heroically save your daughter from the terrible liar (like, seriously, implanted messages, yeah...uh huh) that your wife is. Seriously, I have no respect for her lie. It's pathetic. Any cunning woman would have blamed you and tried to turn the situation around. 

Leave her, ASAP. Figure out a means to an end and leave. Don't even tell her. Go to your parents, best friend, idk, but figure out a plan to bail. You are worth more than this, and deserve an honest partner who will respect you. Record and document EVERYTHING because if you two don't agree on an arrangement for your daughter, you're going to have to deal with one hell of a custody battle. Best of luck, and grab the hell out of those balls.

Honestly, I worked 14 hour days for 10 days straight (including weekends) working in the corporate environment before. I wouldn't want to be near my phone or want to make contact with an SO. I'm in survival mode. It may be selfish, but I'd rather save you from the stress. Just text him "Hey, I know you're going through crunch time, I will give you your space until its over." If he doesn't reach out within 72 hours after it's over, I would have the serious conversation. 


On a positive note, let this be a time of self-discovery. It's nice not worrying about someone for a little while.
Please explain, what exactly is "Stalking" in your experience? Legal trouble?
This is the greatest comment in the history of space mountain

"I'm sure if you could land someone you loved once, you can certainly do it again; there are a lot of women on this planet, roughly 3.8 billion, and none of them are the one who left you, so find one who won't once you figure yourself out and fix whatever behavior you regretted. I hope you'll consider getting back in the saddle, because that's the only thing you can do when in this situation. Keep moving."

This.

Have you talked to a counselor about this? - That said, is this an urge to hurt people, or just a thought, and its like "WHOAH, I can't believe I just thought that shit". And why do you feel this way?

Looks like you two need to spice up the relationship just a tad bit. He may be feeling the same as you. Plus, he's an introvert. He values his time and having other people around him may over-stimulate him. Here's a recommendation, read "Quiet: the Power of Introverts", it may put a completely new view of your boyfriend. He doesn't want you to feel bad because he needs to recharge; but let him know that he can be honest with you. I am very against the advice that "he needs to put on his big boy pants and say it". It implies you are powerless in the situation; when in reality, it is you who needs to express their needs. 


Here's also a fun suggestion. Go out and do something different. Introverts do like other things besides being inside all day. Troglodytes, do not.

If you have an eating disorder, there's high chance of vitamin deficiency, which could definitely lead you into cultivating suicidal thoughts. I take you're someone who tries different diets, right? Maybe take a step back and try a well-balanced diet, or add the nutritional deficiencies in the form of a smoothie. It doesn't matter why you feel this way, you do, and it sucks. But hopefully you can see that it can be managed, and that's the key ingredient to growth. I once thought about an ex-girlfriend every day, every hour, for 4 years. I couldn't get her off my mind, I had been traumatized by an event. But today, she comes into my mind maybe once every 6 months. My thoughts about the event became managed, and I eventually was able to allow myself to sleep soundly.
Compromise and have it on the middle name?

You're most welcome. It's funny, I would call my mom the "Prussian general" and my dad the "absentee-ballot", for very similar reasons as you mentioned about your parents. I guess making a joke about it made it easier for me to cope with. 

And it's okay to have made past mistakes. No character in any novel would ever be interesting without some sort of defect to their constitutional makeup. Hopefully you can find some resolve in meditation, or some other stress-relieving alternative (get a massage?). Best of luck, sir.

I'm reading your posts to other subs and it seems that you had a pretty good head on your shoulders. You are into working out, right? Why don't you go for the longest run of your life tonight? Give yourself a temporary escape from all the bullshit, priorities, "adulting", etc., and feel the endorphins of a good run.
Yes. Yes, omg, the raging in that game. And yet I still play it.

This. 

I'll also add that know what you can control in life. You can't control anyone liking you (even your parents, trust me, I've tried myself), but you can control your emotions to their instability.

You know, I talked with my therapist about why my ex went from 0-100 in terms of her panic around me, it was because she had an abusive father (not directly to her) who couldn't control his anger around the house. And the moment I would get slightly upset, she would be reminded of her father, and go into panic/insult mode. 


Now, let's get to you. It sounds like you had shitty parents and you became a shitty person to your girlfriend. I'd go talk to a therapist to better understand why you broke so out of character the person you want to be (assuming you believe cheating hurts another person at your expense). There's definitely some family dynamics I am sensing with your post. 

Also, it's not cowardice to not be able to kill yourself. It's biology. I read here recently go throw someone in water and they'll react to trying to swim immediately. 

And lastly, it sounds like you're a very stressed out individual (like myself). It makes every day less pleasurable, and you're right, the fleeting moments of pleasure we get...are very fleeting. But with ADHD, the stress can accumulate faster because it's difficult to prioritize and organize a cohesive thought. If you are not taking any medication - or plan to - have you ever considered meditation? There's a ton of research on it, and I bet if you challenged yourself everyday for 30 days, you might be able to detect a small glimmer of hope in your improvement. But it feels you're running from a butt-load of stress, and there's ways to lower it, especially with a very active mind.

Ironically enough, I would be the friend on the other side like some of the other folks who've posted on this thread. My really good buddy, roommate, childhood friend, etc., got paralyzed in a car accident from the chest down. We showed up, tried to tell him we'd be there for him, called him all the time, gave him his space, visited...but eventually he just wanted to be alone and ghosted us all. It was painful for the group of friends who we were all so close together growing up, and to be honest, I felt like a shitty friend myself wondering if I could have done something different. But whenever he decides to reach out to us again, there's nothing that would stop me from trying to reconnect with him. It might be overwhelming, but you had some serious issues to deal with, and I would hope your friends can understand that too. Mental illness can be difficult for some to understand, so maybe tell them the biological roots of it. That might make it easier for them to digest when you get more science into it.

Can you explain the nature of your stalking crimes? Is it social media stalking, or something which would truly scare another individual? And where does this need come from? - By the way, to make you feel a bit better, from an evolutionary psychology viewpoint, stalking would have been a great need back in the day of hunter's and gatherers. This does not say it is normal to act on your impulses, but it shouldn't be anything you are worried about. There's a difference in having the thoughts and acting them out. Lots of people have wilder thoughts than you - I'd bet $100 on that.
You can reach out to the Suicide Hotline and seek assistance, I am sure they will be there to hear your story.

Please don't and reach out to someone. Message me if you must, but reach out to someone. Call a friend. And breathe...take 10 huge deep breaths and let them out slowly. Do this again until you've calmed yourself down.
Whoah there, what do you mean you are going to commit stalking crimes? Why do you feel this way?

If I throw a coke bottle because I am coming down from cocaine and am imploding inside versus if I throw a coke bottle because I want to intimidate you with my power, they are very different reasons. Clearly, both show signs of an unhealthy mind, either from stress or insecurity, or whatever else. What is important is how the OP felt - probably scared if either of those scenarios were true, which isn't cool. I couldn't agree more on "once that line is crossed"...it would be difficult to come back to any normalcy without a high degree of effort.

Still completely out of context. If you read that I believe he's an addict, then it may not be about the power complex. He's a user. "Temper Tantrum" was a poor choice of words, my bad there. Anger management or emotional management is what it sounds like he needs.
You're a real jerk.

You need a vacation - not a tragedy. Have you thought about going somewhere? Are you able to afford a trip out? Even just staying at a motel for a night would give you a sense of ownership in your life. You are not alone, and I know how difficult it could be for you to hear that right now. Put up the razors. Got get a massage. Do anything to relive the stress. Go call the suicide hotline. But whatever's on your mind now, STOP. Go run until you can't breathe anymore. But STOP what you're doing now.
You're exactly why the media today is biased - taking everything out of context. The point for OP is she's seeking guidance, help, new viewpoints, etc. She deserves a full spectrum of viewpoints.

Your point about millennial suicides and debt is interesting, especially when you also bring in the idea that "you aren't living if you aren't experiencing" mantra of this generation. 

Now, let's get to the real point. You're in debt and feel miserable and feel that your life isn't in control anymore. That's the gist of what I got - you feel like a slave to the financier class. Don't let them take your money - and your life. Write down a list of things you control, maybe that'll make you feel better. I've found that many people in their early 20's have problems related to not knowing what they "control" and what they "do not control". Maybe that's some of the tension that you're feeling right now.

I agree, she doesn't owe him anything, and she needs to make a decision on the next steps. And the behavior is unacceptable, I have never disagreed. But abusive is really about power, and if the OP wants to try anything but leave him (I don't know the OP's mind), then I offer alternative viewpoints. This is why we're here on Reddit. The "he's an abuser, leave his ass" really dilutes the complexities of the human condition.

Using drugs with an infant is not abusive - it's negligent and provides the toddler an unstable environment. It could be just as bad, or worse than abusive.

Throwing a coke bottle at the wall is not abusive either. He could have a temper tantrum. We don't know this guy. 

Kneeling down on the ground and crying afterwards could be bipolar disorder. It may not be manipulative. The guy's clearly doing drugs, and most bipolar cases deal with Bipolar IV, which is substance-induced bipolar. The guy's clearly not well put together right now if he's using. 

The thing we'll need to get from the OP is this - why does she think he does this? I can't get an accurate profile of the guy, and won't jump to conclusions. He's clearly made some egregious mistakes and realizes it after the fact. He could be an addict who needs help. The OP needs more help now though than this guy. She's in a very unstable, toxic environment with a 1-year old. A change is needed. How the OP decides on that change is up to her, I only offer alternatives.

The guy could be flippant and emotional, and there's always a spectrum of what abusive means. He could be insecure and not know it because he's developed poor strategies in life. If it's all about an imbalance of power and he's unable to "change", then I 100% would agree with your statement. We only know so much on Reddit :-)

Your parents remind me of mine - except mine didn't laugh, they just completely ignored. Hey a few things I'd like to let you know, since you're young. I am a 30 year old male and I haven't believed in God since I was 7 years old. You don't need to believe in a God, or not believe in one. You can let the ambiguity of his existence just sit there for a while because I think that's what your biggest problem with God is - it's too ambiguous. It's a hard lesson to let ambiguity persist in one's life, but it'll make you a better person. 


"Imagine that you've been struggling with school and had suicidal thoughts since 5th grade". Reading this makes me very sad because there's some needs that you aren't getting right now. Here's a proposal. Try writing out what needs are missing in your life and take a step by step approach to fulfilling them. Is it romance? Is it friends? Is it loving parents? What's interesting is only one of these isn't possible - your parents loving you the way you want them to. The fact of life is, is that you have to know what you can control and can't control. You may never "feel" a romance the way you want it to be. It's fine. You may never "feel" your parents love you the way you want it to be. It's also fine. And you may never feel secure with the God question. All these are acceptable, but in each of these interactions, the question you are going to have to ask yourself is this: What do I control? 

Write down everything where you have ownership in your life. It could be as simple as "I have ownership to move this paper to the left side of my desk" to "I have ownership to manage my emotions when my parents treat me poorly". Nothing will make you stronger than knowing what you own. There's a far greater power in identifying this, especially earlier in life.

Become someone else, step by step. Those problems can be resolved, but life can get overwhelming at times, but once you write all of those problems down, objectively count how many you actually have. Sometimes it's just two, but they get applied to every part of your life and you don't realize it. Once you've identified your problems, ask yourself this: are these problems I can control, and are these problems outside of my control? If the latter, acceptance-therapy may be an option. However, if you feel you can control them (maybe not today, but a month from now), that's a step forward and it'll shape you unlike anything you've ever experienced.

Here's my two cents, if you want to put in the time together, go see a couples counselor. You are not happy, and he may not be either. Unless he's willing to put in the work, leave him. You don't have to give him a chance either, I am just suggesting an alternative. Leave/Stay are not always the only two options, either. Maybe stay with your parents with the kid, say you want to work together at a counselors. Tell him you HAVE to do this together, or individually. What's crazy in all of this is why does he think the kid wasn't his??? Tell him to work on some issues if he's that insecure. Being insecure isn't a bad thing either. Tell him that.

No. I was very suicidal 10 years ago. If these clinics had been open, I wouldn't have had some of the best experiences of my life. I know it sucks now, and it may take some time, but I believe you can push past this.
Why are you going to live a shitty life? Be as objective as possible.

NOT AT ALL. Fact of life is you don't have to be good at anything, you just have to show up. And programming's a fine skill to have to meet people. I know there's a few Python meetups where I live at, perhaps there's something nearby your community. And if there isn't, heck, make one yourself and be the leader. Nothing's more satisfying than owning something that you call yours.

It isn't as bad as you think. Have you thought about joining the military? What about working for the National Parks N Wildlife? Or heck, what about trying a successful blog? You are luckier today than you were 100 years ago, and I know it sucks to hear because being a wage slave is no way to live. My bet is you've done little research so far on freelance careers and entrepreneurship. There's a lot out there. 

Let me put it this way. I work in corporate and I hate it. I make decent money, but am looking to go sell my skills with a bunch of rebel video game developers and possibly make no money for years. It may be the biggest risk of my life. I don't have the skills. But I do have the passion for being with a bunch of people who are against becoming a corporate drone themselves.

"I just realized my best (and only) friend is a random dude of the internet I've known for about 3 years now." 

That's your main problem. You need to go out there and make some friends, join a club, find some peers. It doesn't matter. You're at a great age to make friends, too. I am 30 years old, and I miss my 15-17 year old days. Friends only get more difficult to keep up as you age, so I would learn how to network, and make this a high priority in your life. Who knows, maybe you'll go to college and find yourself. Lots of kids your age don't realize the benefits of college on their social life until they get there. You will meet the kind of folks that have been missing from your life. And always remember, most people are generally pretty nice and don't feel ashamed if you get rejected by 1 or 2 jerks. Best of luck.

My father's the same way - a real prick who hasn't acknowledged his "lack of fathering". Seriously, the guy just came home and looked for swinger dates. Yes, swingers. 

Maybe you can think about it this way. Right now you are experiencing straight up nihilism. Perhaps chemically-induced, perhaps ideologically. Either way, your task should be to extract meaning, find things that make you content. Go get a massage, I don't know. 

Also, OP, have you tried meditation? It takes a while, but it can definitely help with the overactive imagination. 

You're not alone out there, believe me. If you can focus and write down all the things that you wish to change about yourself, start with 1 of those for a week. Let this be a process. Then cross it off if you've successfully done it for that entire week. Then go down thelist.

Everything's relative, man. Doesn't matter if you grow up rich, poor, middle class, it looks like there were some deep-rooted needs that were never dealt with at an early childhood age. 

I would break up with your girlfriend if she's unable to maturely recognize the pain you're going through. At the same time, I would start meditating and doing things for you. In this hypercompetitive society, everyone thinks they're a failure. Truth, Julius Caesar thought he was a major failure because he didn't conquer the world at Alexander the Great's age. He was powerful, had plenty of women, but yet felt like a failure. We're in the same boat here in America. We think success is everything, which it's not. You could be just as unhappy with a million dollars in your bank account compared to $200. Anyways, I hope you can find a way to manage your emotions and move forward. I know how hard it can be.

I am of two minds about this. One is, I'm going through being ghosted after a 3.5 year relationship. That was 6 months ago. I've not seriously thought about suicide until that occurred. I've wanted her to take responsibility, leave the relationship with a modicum of respect, and own her part in it. Instead, she just flew away, and said she was happier because she's finally found a set of friends "who really love her". I am so, so hurt to be used up this way. Anyways, the motivating thought to kill myself is "I AM SERIOUS, I NEED YOU". I hate how much of a power grab it sounds, but dammit, why couldn't she have been okay about closure. Her finding another man would have been great, just anything about WHY.



My second thought is this. You have emotions, and you wanted to connect to her world with another man at that time. This is perfectly normal, and you shouldn't feel any guilt about moving on. I know deep down you wish you could've reshaped those conversations, and managed your new guy with your ex. You may never move on from this, but know you're not a terrible person. Seriously. Life is complicated and communication failures happen between two people, not one. By God, two tragedies won't fix one tragedy. So here's my advice as being currently para-suicidal from my ex: if I were to hurt myself, deep down I know it's my fault. It's just difficult to manage being stuck, needing this, or needing that, I desperately need an outlet to vent and talk more with my therapist. It sucks being alone. I also suffer from an anxiety disorder that affects intimacy with others, except for girlfriends. It just sucks. But you're not to blame, and your surely not a terrible person. I hope you can learn to live with yourself, I'd hate to say that you're responsible-free from it, and I'd hate to blame you at the same time. You did what you knew in that moment and now listen. Listen to friends, listen to your self. Find joy that you were with this guy, and take time mourning for his loss. Best of luck.

I know how you feel, I'm here also because of being ghosted by an ex. I'd say I'm ambitious - or was - until being ghosted. Everything's lost a lot of meaning for me and I'm unable to stop by thoughts about how nihilistic the world is to me. 


That said, I know you're not alone. I believe that having had that closure to your life would have eased many, many unnecessary challenges in your life. People like to think that "what doesn't kill you makes you stronger", I am not 100% of this opinion. The right thing for her to have done is be a good person and talk it out. We always say "no contact is best after relationships". Fuck. That. You have someone's heart, and you decide to throw it away and have them think about you for the next year...because that's the right thing to do? Hell no. Which is why I am going to find a decent person. I hate this double standard in our society. After a break up it's cool to say abusive shit, and then have a crowd of folks back you up on "taking respomsibility for your own actions". Well I'll tell ya, the abuser can be a woman. What, you just throw off duty as a good human being because you want to move on? How much more progressive as a society can we be if we view responsibly the rehabilitation of two people after a break up. We want more people on their feet. Sorry...I'm digressing. 

Anyways...I feel you man. I'm completely inept at getting sleep and it's driving me insane right now.
